- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3%.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2%.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; delay correction until sentiment stabilizes or add 0.5–1.0% downward bias.
- In low-volatility periods (sentiment flat or mixed), model tends to over-smooth; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to avoid underprediction.
- When sentiment history includes multiple -1.00 entries, model often underreacts to bearish signals; increase downward bias by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
